chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the carriers (porters) who hire out their beasts of burden. I said, 'They change (their location/route) every day; whenever something comes to them, they change.' He said, 'There is negligence upon them if they travel.'

key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: Beasts of burden (animals used for carrying loads)
key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: Carriers or porters who hire out beasts of burden

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on carriers who frequently change their location while traveling?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses the specific legal status of carriers (*al-mukarin*) who frequently change locations while engaged in their trade. The Imam rules that they are subject to *al-taqsir* (shortening of prayer) during travel, highlighting the Shia juristic principle that frequent, irregular movement prevents one from being classified as a settled resident (*muqim*), thereby maintaining the traveler's status for prayer and fasting purposes.
